title: Can meal prep portions be adjusted for kids?
meta_title: Meal Prep Portions for Kids: What to Agree | myCHEF
meta_description: Yes — agree children's meal-prep portions by appetite and routine, not age. A briefing table, packing options and a review method for Dubai households.
excerpt: How to brief children's portions for chef-cooked meal prep: what to agree, how to pack and how to review after the first meals.
body_html:
Yes. Meal-prep portions can be adjusted for children, and the adjustment works best when you brief it as serving instructions rather than asking for a smaller adult plate. Start from what each child usually eats, agree which components are packed separately, and say how extra food is stored and offered. If you are arranging weekly cooking through our private chef service in Dubai, include these points in the household brief so the first cooking session starts with them settled.

What to agree before the first cooking session

A short table of instructions prevents most portioning misunderstandings:

Detail to agreeWhy it mattersExample instruction
Usual servingPortions follow appetite, not ageHalf the usual rice, full chicken piece
Components kept separateLets a caregiver assemble the plateSauce in its own pot, never mixed in
Containers and labellingPrevents confusion at serving timeNames on containers or two clear zones
Extra portionsMore food is available without pressureSpare rice kept in a separate tub
Who servesInstructions must make sense to that personHousehold helper serves the children's plates

Three ways to pack a child's meal

Choose the packing format around how the meal will actually be served:

FormatWorks well whenWatch out for
Individually packed mealA caregiver serves a ready plateHard to adjust once everything is mixed
Separately packed componentsComponents need different quantitiesMore containers and clearer instructions
Shared family dishesEveryone eats together at the tableSomeone must portion at mealtime

Preferences, requirements and professional advice

  • Separate dislike from requirement. A disliked sauce needs a swap; a medical restriction needs written detail from the child's healthcare professional.
  • Keep allergy instructions in writing. Removing one ingredient from a finished dish is not an allergy-management process; ask the chef what preparation steps are actually possible in your kitchen.
  • Share professional guidance. If a clinician has set feeding or nutrition instructions, pass the food-relevant parts to the chef so the cooking follows them.

A worked review after the first week (hypothetical)

A household with two children receives the first week of chef-cooked meals. One child clears the main but leaves a mixed-in sauce; the other eats roughly half the starting pasta. The feedback sent back is one line per child: keep the main and pack the sauce separately for the first; start with a smaller pasta serving and keep extra available for the second. The next cooking session changes only those two instructions. This example is hypothetical; it illustrates the review method, not a recorded booking.

What to send with your enquiry

  • Each child's usual servings and any foods to keep separate.
  • Written dietary requirements and any professional instructions that affect cooking.
  • Who serves each meal, and when it is eaten.
  • Container preferences and how extra portions should be stored.

To plan household meal prep around your family's portions, send your requirements through our private chef page together with the household brief. For budget context, the weekly meal-prep quote guide explains what a quote should include.
